title: Competence lifts output level smoothly while coordination governs scale—and swarms still hit diminishing returns
text: Decomposing organizational capability into competence (output per worker at fixed size) and coordination (returns to adding members) explains why current agent deployments hit a ceiling. Individual model competence is rising rapidly, yet multi-agent coordination remains below the 'supercooperative' threshold—illustrated by Noam Brown’s observation attributing under 10% credit to multi-agent coordination on open math problems—so spinning up larger agent swarms quickly runs into diminishing returns.
qualification: Qualitative frontier observation paired with an organizational scaling-law model; future advances in shared state, context passing, or agent protocols could shift the coordination curve.

public_locator.value: AI models are getting exponentially better in individual competence while lagging behind in coordination. Across dozens of professions, models already match or outperform experienced specialists on self-contained deliverables. Spin up a swarm of agents, however, and output still runs quickly into diminishing returns.
